description: AquaByte is a multidisciplinary team passionate about space, Earth observation, software, and scientific problem-solving. We turn NASA data into practical solutions using remote sensing, GIS, data science, ML, and modern technology. We welcome teammates skilled or interested in Python, geospatial science, ML, web development, UI/UX, research, data analysis, and storytelling.
summary:
Earth Whisper is an Earth-observation platform developed by Team Aquabyte for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Dancing with the SARs." Its main solution, DHARA, brings satellite imagery, fisheries-related information and AI-based screening together in one interactive investigation platform.

Using ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery, DHARA identifies possible areas of water increase and decrease. It also uses Sentinel-1 radar observations with two experimental AI models, Attention U-Net and ResNet50, to compare possible water-change patterns. Historical aquaculture mapping provides additional fisheries context. We also integrated NASA-ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV observations as a separate regional radar data stream.

Using a reported embankment failure at Pallimangal Fisheries Enclosure, Jashore, as an investigation case, DHARA demonstrates how different satellite observations can be explored together. By making complex data easier to understand, DHARA helps identify areas that may need closer investigation and supports more focused fisheries and environmental decision-making.
details:
Earth Whisper is an interactive Earth-observation platform developed by Team Aquabyte for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing "Dancing with the SARs." Its main solution, DHARA, combines satellite imagery, fisheries-related information and AI-based screening to investigate possible environmental changes.

DHARA uses ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery from January 10 and January 20, 2026, to identify possible water changes using NDWI and MNDWI. The analysis identified 671 possible-new-water cells and 1,316 possible-water-loss candidate cells on a 20-metre grid. These are exploratory signals, not confirmed flood measurements.

The platform also uses Sentinel-1 VV/VH radar observations with two experimental models: Residual Attention U-Net and a ResNet50 encoder-decoder. Historical aquaculture mapping provides additional context for fisheries-related investigations.

We integrated NASA-ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV observations from October 23 and November 4, 2026, as a separate regional radar observation stream, not as evidence of the January incident.

DHARA presents these different sources through interactive maps, evidence previews and model comparisons. Its purpose is to help users understand possible water changes and identify locations that may deserve closer investigation before field visits.

The platform uses React, TypeScript, Leaflet, Python, FastAPI and PyTorch. Its focus is combining different satellite observations with transparent evidence and accessible visual explanations.
